description: The Geo-Disasters research team publishes Python scripts that geocode climate-related EM-DAT records and join them to GAUL administrative areas. A staged workflow selects events missing geographic identifiers, queries GeoNames, cleans matches, assigns quality flags, creates national overlays and exports spatial data. The documented application covers global events during 1990–2023. GitHub provides the README, dependencies and ordered scripts, while Figshare archives a ZIP snapshot under MIT. Source access is open and free. The README documents Python 3.8.19 and separate R scripts for publication figures. Required EM-DAT and GAUL inputs are not supplied; their access and licensing must be checked separately. GeoNames requires a valid account identifier, has request limits and can take days for the full batch. Manual corrections remain necessary, so this is not an automatically verified geocoder. Modellers could use the workflow to prepare event locations for exposure comparisons and impact simulations. It complements the finished Geo-Disasters dataset by making the processing route inspectable. Nothing was installed or executed.
